claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock has a homogeneous composition.
Rapid cooling during processing makes AlCrFeNiSi susceptible to segregation, residual stress, and defect formation.
The proposed intervention is in-situ preheating of the LPBF substrate and surrounding powder bed to 300–500 °C.
Substrate preheating will reduce thermal gradients during LPBF solidification.
Preheating lowers the temperature differential between the molten pool and surrounding material.
The lower temperature differential moderates the cooling rate.
Reduced thermal gradients and moderated cooling will produce finer, more uniform grains.
Moderated cooling will reduce elemental or phase segregation, including segregation at grain boundaries.
Preheating will reduce processing-induced porosity and cracking.
Preheating will lower residual stress in LPBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The resulting homogeneous, low-stress microstructure will improve mechanical integrity.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have higher yield strength than non-preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than non-preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stress, pronounced segregation, and a higher defect density.
The proposed comparison is valid under inert-atmosphere LPBF with otherwise identical standard laser parameters.
Mechanical-property comparisons are bounded to room-temperature, quasi-static testing.
Application to other additive-manufacturing methods or substantially different alloy compositions requires further validation.
